Source files must not contain newline characters after the final code token.

What The Standard says

“Readability” — The Standard favors readable, standardized code over incidental implementation choices. A deterministic final token boundary removes invisible file-ending variation between otherwise identical sources. read it here.
“consistent handling” — The Standard's canonical implementations explicitly value consistency across methods. This analyser applies the same consistency principle to the end of every source file. read it here.

Why it matters

The Standard values consistency and immediate readability; trailing blank lines add no meaning and produce noisy diffs. Enforcing a clean final token gives every source file a predictable ending without changing the code's behaviour.

Bad code example

// Violates STXFORMAT001: Source files must not contain newline characters after the final code token.
class Student { }

Good code example

// Follows STXFORMAT001
class Student { }
